meta.title: nr-mcp-agent — a controlled AI assistant for the TYPO3 backend
meta.description: A backend assistant that reads by default and asks for a human approval before it writes. Alpha: for controlled evaluation, not for unattended production use.
meta.ogImageAlt: nr-mcp-agent — a controlled AI assistant for the TYPO3 backend

hero.title: A controlled AI assistant for the TYPO3 backend.
hero.lead: Editors ask in the backend they already work in. The assistant reads what they may already see, and asks for an explicit approval before it changes anything.
hero.alphaNote: For controlled evaluation, not for unattended production use. Interfaces, tool contracts and configuration can still change between releases.
hero.ctaBusiness: Evaluate a backend agent under control

status.heading: Status
status.note: Latest release and main branch are different values, and the review date is a third. A difference between them is not a contradiction.

answers.heading: What you can tell in ten seconds
answers.lead: The six questions an evaluator asks first, answered before you scroll.

items.a: Alpha. Evaluate it with someone watching.
Read by default. Writing tools ship disabled.
Before every write. The run suspends until someone approves or rejects.
Prompt injection, a wrong proposal approved without reading it, and too large a tool set.
Per-group tool release, TYPO3 permissions, and nr-llm's budgets.
Install it, point it at an nr-llm configuration, release a read-only tool group.

works.heading: What works today
works.lead: Stated as what it does, not as what it will do.

items.title: Backend chat
items.body: A conversation in the TYPO3 backend, for the user who is signed in. No separate tool, no separate login.

items.title: Retrieving information
items.body: The assistant can look things up through the tools an administrator released, and summarise what it found.

items.title: Released MCP tools only
items.body: Tools are configured per server and per permission. Nothing is available by default; the empty set is the starting point.

items.title: Conversation history
items.body: A run can be re-read afterwards. Without that there is nothing to review.

items.title: Known content operations
items.body: The content operations documented for the current release, each one either read-only or approval-gated. The documentation lists them; this page does not restate the list, because a list restated is a list that goes stale.

notPromised.heading: What is not promised
notPromised.lead: Five things the extension does not do. If you need one of them, this is the wrong tool today.
items: Autonomous CMS operation. It has no schedule, no trigger and no unattended mode.
Unrestricted write access. Writing tools are released per group and gated per call.
Automatic approval. There is no timeout that approves on your behalf.
A faultless substitute for an editor. It proposes; a person decides.
Unreviewed actions. Everything that changes something leaves an audit record with the approver's decision.

scenarios.heading: Three controlled scenarios
scenarios.lead: In order of how much trust each one needs.

items.title: Find and summarise
items.body: Ask where a topic is covered across the pages the acting user may see, and get a summary with the records it came from.
items.control: Read-only tools. No approval needed, because nothing changes.

items.title: Prepare a change
items.body: Ask for a proposed rewrite, a translation or a set of alt texts. The result is a proposal in the conversation, not an edit.
items.control: Still read-only. The editor copies what they want, or asks for another version.

items.title: Execute an approved change
items.body: With a writing tool released, the assistant proposes the exact change and waits. On approval it executes; on rejection it stops.
items.control: Approval gate, audit record, TYPO3 permissions. The approver reads the proposal — that is the control, and skipping it removes it.

permissions.heading: Who may do what
permissions.lead: Six layers, each of which can stop a run on its own.

rows.effect: Whether the person may use the assistant at all.
Which MCP tools exist for that group. The default is none.
Whether a tool changes anything. Writing tools ship disabled.
Whether a specific write actually happens, decided by a person, per call.
Whether the record is reachable for the acting user. Not bypassed.
What happened afterwards: tool, user, arguments, decision.

permissions.cancel: A rejected approval stops the run and records the rejection. A failing tool call surfaces the error rather than retrying silently, and a run that exceeds its nr-llm budget stops with an explicit reason.

stack.heading: How it relates to nr-llm
stack.lead: This extension is the agent interface. nr-llm is the controlled AI base underneath it.

items.title: Provider and model
items.body: Chosen in nr-llm. This extension holds no key and talks to no provider directly.

items.title: Budgets
items.body: nr-llm's per-user request, token and cost limits apply to agent runs like any other AI use.

items.title: Cost analytics
items.body: Agent usage shows up in the same analytics as every other AI feature on the site.

items.title: Fallbacks
items.body: Provider fallback chains are configured once in nr-llm and apply here too.

items.title: Where the boundary is
items.body: nr-mcp-agent decides what the agent may attempt. nr-llm decides which model answers, at what cost, for whom.

security.heading: Security
security.lead: The risks an agent brings, named rather than implied.

items.title: Excessive agency
items.body: The most common failure of an agent is being allowed to do too much. Release the smallest useful tool set; the default of none exists for that reason.

items.title: Prompt injection
items.body: Content the agent reads can contain instructions. The tool release list and the approval gate bound the damage; they do not prevent the attempt.

items.title: Tool poisoning
items.body: A tool description is part of the model's input. Release tools from sources you control, and read what a tool declares before releasing it.

items.title: Data disclosure
items.body: The agent can only reach what the acting user may reach. That makes the acting user's permissions the disclosure boundary — review them before you widen access.

items.title: Permission escalation
items.body: Approval is per call and cannot be delegated to the agent. An approver who approves without reading is the escalation path that remains.

items.title: Cost and resource limits
items.body: nr-llm's budgets apply. A run that exceeds them stops with an explicit reason rather than continuing quietly.

items.title: Logging and traceability
items.body: Tool, user, arguments and decision are recorded for every call, which is what makes an after-the-fact review possible.

evidence.heading: Evidence

items.title: Source code

limits: No conformity claim for the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or ISO/IEC 42001. The extension supports controls; whether an organisation is conformant is a legal and organisational assessment.
No productivity or savings figure. We do not know your editorial volumes.
No guarantee about model behaviour. The controls bound what the agent may do, not what the model may say.

install.heading: Trying it out
install.lead: Four steps. Stop after the third if you only want to see what it reads.

steps.title: Point it at nr-llm
steps.body: Choose an existing nr-llm configuration. Provider, model and budget come from there.

steps.title: Release a read-only tool group
steps.body: Start with the smallest set that makes the assistant useful for one task.

steps.title: Only then consider a writing tool
steps.body: Release it for one group, on one kind of record, and read what it proposes before approving.
